Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Krishna reveals that a truly wise person sees inaction in action and action in inaction, staying spiritually grounded while engaging in all kinds of activities.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The illusion that physical movement always equals binding work, or that physical stillness equals true rest/liberation.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna asserts: 'karmany akarma yah pasyed akarmani ca karma yah, sa buddhiman manusyesu sa yuktah krtsna-karma-krt' (One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is intelligent among people and integrated in all deeds).
Outcome/Resolution: Redefines action based on internal detachment rather than external motion, fostering deep peace amid active life.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Inner Calm in Outer Activity: Maintaining emotional equilibrium while fully engaged in work
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Paradoxical Thinking: Understanding that outer motion can coexist with inner stillness
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mindful Engagement: Acting without internal stress or compulsive attachment

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Akarmani ca karma (Hidden psychological action within physical stillness)
Yuktah krtsna-karma-krt (Balanced and fully accomplished in action)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Detached action yields no karmic reaction (inaction in action), whereas suppressed physical activity with selfish desire remains binding work (action in inaction).
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Busy work done with an unattached mind creates zero mental stress, while passive physical avoidance accompanied by mental obsession remains highly exhausting.
